variants.headline: Home-world ship reaches the colony
variants.sub: The colony has received the arrival of a home-world ship.
variants.body:
A ship from the home world has arrived in {colony}. The arrival is a concrete event in the colony's connection with its distant origin. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that fact from assumptions about particular goods, passengers or immediate changes in local supply not specified in this report.

An arrival is a logistics fact, not a completed account of supply and demand. Commercial readers should distinguish the vessel reaching the colony from delivery, settlement or the sale of particular goods. Sound planning requires the actual cargo and transaction record rather than an assumed benefit attached to the ship itself.

We remain critical of {target}. An arrival should not place the stewardship of the colony's transport connection beyond scrutiny; the existence of a ship is not a complete account of responsible provision. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
